sn44.7:5.3: “Worthy Gotama, is this right: ‘the cosmos is eternal’?”
sn44.7:5.4: “Vaccha, this has not been declared by me: ‘the cosmos is eternal’ …
sn44.7:5.5: “Then, worthy Gotama, is this right: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?”
sn44.7:5.6: “This too has not been declared by me:
sn44.7:5.7: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’”
sn44.7:6.1: “What’s the cause, worthy Gotama, what’s the reason why, when the wanderers of other religions are asked these questions, they declare:
sn44.7:6.3: or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?
sn44.7:6.4: And what’s the reason why, when the worthy Gotama is asked these questions, he does not declare:
sn44.7:6.6: or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?”
sn44.7:7.1: “Vaccha, the wanderers of other religions regard the eye like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’ …
sn44.7:7.2: They regard the tongue like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’ …
sn44.7:7.3: mind like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’
sn44.7:7.4: That’s why, when asked, they declare:
sn44.7:7.6: or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’
sn44.7:7.7: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha regards the eye like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’ …
sn44.7:7.8: He regards the tongue like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’ …
sn44.7:7.9: mind like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
sn44.7:7.10: That’s why, when asked, he does not declare:
sn44.7:7.11: ‘the cosmos is eternal’, ‘the cosmos is not eternal’, ‘the cosmos is finite’, ‘the cosmos is infinite’, ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’, ‘the soul is one thing, the body another’, ‘a realized one still exists after death’, ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’, ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’, or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’.”
